headline: Adobe adds AI assistant to Premiere, Illustrator, and InDesign
summary: Adobe's Firefly AI is now integrated into its flagship creative apps, offering generative fill and other AI-powered features directly within your workflow.
details: Adobe has announced the integration of its Firefly generative AI model into its popular creative suite applications, including Premiere Pro, Illustrator, and InDesign. This move aims to bring powerful AI capabilities directly into the hands of creators, streamlining workflows and enhancing creative possibilities.

The new AI features allow users to generate content based on text prompts, such as creating custom vectors in Illustrator or filling in missing parts of images in Photoshop. The AI assistant can also remember the visual style of your creations, enabling consistent design across different projects.

In Premiere Pro, the AI assistant can help with tasks like generating video footage or creating visual effects. For InDesign users, it can assist in generating text and layouts, making the design process more efficient.

Adobe emphasizes that Firefly is designed to be commercially safe, trained on Adobe Stock images, openly licensed content, and public domain content where copyright has expired. This ensures that the generated content can be used responsibly by creators.

The company is also launching a new 'AI Studio' within Adobe Express, which acts as a central hub for accessing and experimenting with Firefly's capabilities. This studio allows users to generate images and text effects, and then easily apply them to their projects across the Creative Cloud ecosystem.

The integration of AI into these professional creative tools marks a significant step in how digital content will be produced. Adobe's approach focuses on augmenting human creativity rather than replacing it, providing tools that help creators work faster and explore new artistic directions.
